researcher: Codex parallel kyrgyzstan-tajikistan research, integrated by Codex

sources.title: Kyrgyz Republic Ministry of Justice, Declaration on State Independence, 31 August 1991
sources.note: Original official legal record checked: Declaration No. 578-XII, adopted 31 August 1991. The record establishes the founding date; later celebratory language is not used as independent evaluation.

sources.title: United Nations Human Rights Committee, second periodic report of Kyrgyzstan
sources.note: Original UN-hosted state report checked, PDF pp. 3-4, paragraphs 6 and 11-14: March 2005 resignation, 7 April 2010 revolution, Bakiyev resignation, interim government, 2010 Constitution and parliamentary system. The report is the government submission and its political praise is not adopted.

sources.title: OSCE ODIHR, preliminary findings on the 15 October 2017 presidential election
sources.note: Original observer statement checked: competitive election and orderly transfer from one elected president to another, alongside pressure, vote-buying, public-resource and count concerns.

sources.title: OSCE ODIHR, Kyrgyzstan 2021 presidential election final report summary
sources.note: Original ODIHR summary checked: 10 January 2021 election and simultaneous referendum, one candidate dominant, uneven resources, generally respected freedoms and weakened public debate. The related report records the annulled 2020 parliamentary vote and transition.

sources.title: Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic, Constitution in Kyrgyz
sources.note: Original current official Kyrgyz text checked: title, preamble and Article 1. The page supplies the authentic Cyrillic wording; the English rendering in the card is a close editorial translation checked against the official English presidency version.

sources.title: Administration of the President of the Kyrgyz Republic, official current site, September 2026
sources.note: Original official presidency site checked on 27 September 2026: its September 2026 calendar and dated current items identify Sadyr Japarov as President. Used only for the time-bounded officeholder identification, not for an independent judgment of his government.

sources.title: OSCE ODIHR, preliminary findings on Kyrgyzstan early parliamentary elections, 1 December 2025
sources.note: Original dated observer release checked: 30 November 2025 election, efficient administration, restrictive campaign environment, declining practical freedoms, weakened party role and incomplete transparency. These are observer findings, not a timeless label.

sources.title: World Bank, Kyrgyz Republic overview, updated 2026
sources.note: Original current country page checked: 2025 growth, inflation, gold, remittances, services, literacy and human-capital assessment, with exposure to commodity and external shocks. Forecasts are not presented as completed outcomes.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sulaiman-Too Sacred Mountain
sources.note: Original World Heritage entry checked: Osh setting, Silk Roads, sacred use for at least 1,500 years, petroglyphs, worship sites, reconstructed mosques and vulnerability to nearby development. This is older heritage on modern territory, not a work built by the 1991 republic.

sources.title: UNESCO, Nomad games: rediscovering heritage, celebrating diversity
sources.note: Original UNESCO good-practice entry checked: post-1991 community revival, 2007 practitioner meeting, first World Nomad Games in 2014, knowledge exchange and safeguarding rather than a claim that every game is uniquely Kyrgyz.

sources.title: UNESCO, Ala-kiyiz and Shyrdak art of Kyrgyz traditional felt carpets
sources.note: Original UNESCO urgent-safeguarding entry checked: household warmth and decoration, communal work, family transmission by older women, declining practitioners and raw-material and synthetic-carpet pressures.

sources.title: UNESCO, traditional knowledge and skills in making Kyrgyz, Kazakh and Karakalpak yurts
sources.note: Original 2025 multinational entry checked: collapsible frame, felt covering, gendered craft roles as documented, family and apprentice transmission, ceremonies and yurts kept as family relics. The account is limited to practising communities.

sources.title: UNESCO, Ak-kalpak craftsmanship
sources.note: Original 2019 entry checked: white felt, felting and embroidery, more than eighty documented kinds, pattern meanings, community workshops and hands-on transmission. Symbolic meanings are reported as community interpretations.

sources.title: UNICEF Kyrgyzstan, Progress in Education, 29 November 2024
sources.note: Original dated release checked: three-year post-pandemic programme, computers, training for 10,300 teachers, 20,500 Grade 5 and 6 pupils and measured test-score gains. Results describe programme participants, not every school.

sources.title: UNICEF Kyrgyzstan, Libraries are transforming into hubs for early childhood development, 18 February 2025
sources.note: Original profile checked: Altynai, a late-2024 village centre, 26 children there, trained librarians and educators, and 300 centres in public libraries. The story also records unequal preschool access.

sources.title: UNICEF Kyrgyzstan, Delivering measles vaccines on horseback, 10 April 2025
sources.note: Original field story checked: nurse Jiydegul Rysbaeva, more than 36 years of service, 41 remote farmsteads, horseback travel, vaccine counselling and wolves. One worker illustrates mountain access; it is not national coverage data.

sources.title: UNICEF Kyrgyzstan, Water, sanitation and hygiene
sources.note: Original current programme page checked: 2023 MICS water figures, about one fifth of households on centralized sewerage, rural reliance on onsite systems, school toilet privacy and safety gaps, and work on locally affordable latrine designs.

sources.title: United States Office of the Historian, Tajikistan recognition history
sources.note: Original official history page checked: Tajikistan was formerly a constituent Soviet republic, became independent in 1991 and received United States recognition on 25 December. Recognition date is not presented as the declaration date.

sources.title: United Nations Peacekeeping, UNMOT background and the Tajik civil war
sources.note: Original UN mission history checked: Supreme Soviet independence vote on 9 September 1991, crisis and tensions, violence from 1992, displacement and deaths, negotiations and final assessment. Dated UN estimates are identified as estimates.

sources.title: United Nations Peacemaker, General Agreement on Peace and National Accord in Tajikistan
sources.note: Original UN-hosted agreement checked, pp. 1-2: signed in Moscow on 27 June 1997 after UN-sponsored talks begun in April 1994; parties were the Government and United Tajik Opposition. Signing is distinguished from later implementation.

sources.title: United Nations Peacekeeping, UNMOT mandate and peace implementation
sources.note: Original mission mandate checked: Security Council establishment in December 1994, expanded mandate after the 27 June 1997 agreement, support for reconciliation, elections, demobilization and reintegration through mission completion in 2000.

sources.title: OSCE ODIHR, final report summary on Tajikistan parliamentary elections, 15 May 2015
sources.note: Original ODIHR summary checked: restrictions on candidacy, association and expression, limited reform and recommendations. The item describes observer findings rather than treating an election as proof of democratic performance.

sources.title: OSCE ODIHR, Tajikistan presidential election 2020 final report summary
sources.note: Original dated ODIHR summary checked: peaceful voting in a tightly controlled environment without pluralistic debate or genuine alternatives. The linked report records wide presidential powers and the 2016 incumbent exemption from consecutive-term limits.

sources.title: OSCE ODIHR, cancellation of Tajikistan 2025 election observation mission
sources.note: Original 4 February 2025 release checked: observer mission cancelled after accreditation assurances were not supplied; prior needs assessment recorded concerns about institutional independence and deteriorating expression, association and assembly. This does not substitute for an observation of election day.

sources.title: President of the Republic of Tajikistan, participation in Central Asia-Republic of Korea summit, 16 September 2026
sources.note: Original dated official presidency record checked: the 16 September 2026 summit item identifies Emomali Rahmon as President of the Republic of Tajikistan. Used only for the time-bounded officeholder identification, not for the page's political praise or policy claims.

sources.title: National Center of Legislation under the President of Tajikistan, Constitution in Tajik
sources.note: Original current official legal text checked: adopted 6 November 1994, amendments in 1999, 2003 and 2016, preamble and Articles 1-2. The translation in the card is editorial and the legal promises are not treated as measured outcomes.

sources.title: World Bank, Tajikistan overview, updated 2026
sources.note: Original current country page checked: 2025 growth and poverty estimates, services and agriculture, remittances near 46 per cent of GDP, trade deficit and vulnerability. Forecasts and policy ambitions are not presented as completed results.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Proto-urban Site of Sarazm
sources.note: Original World Heritage entry checked: fourth to third millennia BCE settlement, pastoral and agricultural links, metallurgy, long-distance exchange, modern reserve status and remaining management fragility. Ancient achievements are not reassigned to the 1991 state.

sources.title: United Nations in Tajikistan, interview on the High-Level Conference on Glaciers Preservation, 28 May 2025
sources.note: Original dated UN country-team interview checked: Tajikistan promoted the initiative behind the UN International Year of Glaciers Preservation 2025 and hosted the Dushanbe conference; goals are cooperation and resource mobilization, not proof that melting has stopped.

sources.title: World Bank, Rogun Hydropower Plant Project FAQ
sources.note: Original current project FAQ checked: construction and financing status, projected electricity benefits, debt and transparency concerns, safeguards, benefit sharing and planned resettlement of more than 50,000 people. Expected results are labelled as expectations.

sources.title: UNESCO, Oshi Palav and its social and cultural contexts in Tajikistan
sources.note: Original UNESCO element entry checked: rice, vegetables, meat and spices, up to 200 varieties, household and teahouse groups, music and conversation, family and apprentice transmission, and the symbolic slotted-spoon gift.

sources.title: UNESCO, Chakan embroidery art in the Republic of Tajikistan
sources.note: Original UNESCO Spanish entry checked against its English indexed text: coloured embroidery on clothing and household textiles, bridal use, family and master-student transmission and artisan income. Practices are not universalized to all women or weddings.

sources.title: UNESCO, Falak
sources.note: Original 2021 entry checked: mountain-community music, solo and ensemble forms, themes of separation and reunion, field and herding contexts, festivities and transmission in families and formal education.

sources.title: UNICEF Tajikistan, Creating an inclusive environment for school readiness, 2024
sources.note: Original field profile checked: tutor Alambi, 30 children aged three to six, Umarjon, combined indoor and outdoor activities, and a programme for more than 200 centres with disability inclusion. This is programme scope, not achieved nationwide inclusion.

sources.title: UNICEF Tajikistan, TOMAKTABI.TJ early childhood platform launch
sources.note: Original 2022 launch release checked: platform resources for educators, parents and children and stated aim to benefit 1.5 million children. Aim is not rewritten as verified reach.

sources.title: UNICEF Tajikistan, A Vaccine Hero, 19 April 2024
sources.note: Original field story checked: vaccinator Dilbar Khalimova, family doctors, cold-chain refrigerator checks, immunization passports and parent counselling. One clinic profile illustrates practice, not every clinic.

sources.title: WHO Europe, Tajikistan tests health-financing reforms in Sughd, 11 August 2025
sources.note: Original dated WHO release checked: January 2025 pilot, pooled budgets, purchasing body, per-capita finance, benefits package and facility autonomy, with early indications. A regional pilot is not nationwide universal coverage.

sources.title: UNICEF Tajikistan, Safe environment for every child
sources.note: Original current programme page checked: seismic exposure, lack of piped school water, pit latrines, older pupils avoiding toilets, girls affected by privacy and menstrual-hygiene gaps, and resilience and WASH work. Survey dates remain explicit where used.

sources.title: UNICEF Tajikistan, Clean Water and Safe Care, 25 August 2026
sources.note: Original dated photo essay checked: assessment across 3,297 health facilities, 36 per cent with basic water, 1 per cent meeting basic sanitation and 12 per cent with soap handwashing stations; six named village primary-care centres rehabilitated. National baseline and project result are kept distinct.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Modern Kyrgyz Republic only. Historical independence declaration: 31 August 1991; imported index onset: 1994. Three identical polygon features cover 1994-2000, 2000-2010 and 2010-2020 while the civilization record remains open. Tested included points: Bishkek, Osh, Naryn, Karakol and Batken. Tested excluded foreign points: Almaty, Tashkent and Kashgar. Bounds are [69.34929349293495,39.229606913657854,80.2790027900279,43.205389784023886]. No alias to the Kyrgyz SSR, earlier Kyrgyz polities, nomadic communities or every Kyrgyz-speaking population. The 1994 and 2020 map dates are data coverage, not founding or collapse.

Modern Republic of Tajikistan only. Historical independence vote: 9 September 1991; imported index onset: 1994. Three identical polygon features cover 1994-2000, 2000-2010 and 2010-2020 while the civilization record remains open. Tested included points: Dushanbe, Khujand, Khorugh, Panjakent and Kulob. Tested excluded foreign points: Samarkand, Tashkent and Kabul. Bounds are [67.50967509675098,36.701975373312756,75.00855008550087,41.06877306759957]. No alias to the Tajik SSR, Samanid state, ancient Sarazm, every Tajik-speaking community or neighbouring Persianate polities. The 1994 and 2020 map dates are data coverage, not founding or collapse.
